$comment: Phillip Jeffries (luxury wallcoverings) runs a Rails site whose product page is an AngularJS app: the server HTML carries the product h1 (directly in main) and the <head> metadata, while the breadcrumb, specifications, stock and order panels are {{ }} templates filled in by JavaScript from an API. Product URLs are /shop/<collection code>/<item number> (for example /shop/CARD-464/46400; about 5,500 in sitemap.xml); /shop/<word> pages are listings. Prices and stock are shown only to signed-in trade accounts, so price and availability are not configured and every product returns price.state unknown with a PRICE_MISSING warning; price_unit usd only keeps currency USD. Title is the h1 ('Meta Metallic in Gold Wallcovering - 46400'), image is og:image (Bynder, 1200 px), description is the meta description (collection copy); root is the document because og:image and the description live in <head>. There is no canonical link (og:url is the same URL). Specs are not configured: even in Chrome the Specifications panel renders its labels (Width, Status, Bolt Size, Repeat, Fire Rating, ...) without values for an anonymous visitor. Engines tried on the sample on 2026-11-19: http: SUCCESS with title, image and description; browser: the same, slower; duckduckgo, mojeek, yandex: SEARCH_PROVIDER_BLOCKED; yahoo: SEARCH_PROVIDER_ERROR; brave: not tried, no key; ai-crawler-avalai: the same three fields at 4,529+356 tokens; ai-crawler-cloudflare: not configured. http is selected: the same data at no cost. Checked against saved (curl) Meta Metallic in Gold (46400) and Ripples in Paneled Taupe (9270-A) pages on 2026-11-19.
